Our Business." and the vanity number 855-BYE-BUSH, billboards are now appearing across Tampa Bay, Palm Beach, the Treasure Coast and Fort Lauderdale, challenging conventional pricing practices within the laser hair removal industry.

Refresh's eight-treatment laser hair removal packages start at $460. Its flagship campaign offer includes eight full Brazilian and eight underarm laser hair removal treatments for $580, payable in full or through eight equal monthly payments.

"For far too long, patients pursuing laser hair removal have encountered ambiguous pricing structures and disproportionate financial obligations," said Jay Feinberg, Chief Executive Officer of Refresh – Aesthetics & Wellness. "We fundamentally reject the premise that clinical excellence must come at an exorbitant cost. Our commitment is to the integrity of the patient experience, the sophistication of our clinical protocols and the transparency of our pricing. The billboard is bold because the standard behind it is."

Across its nine Florida locations, Refresh delivers laser hair removal under physician-led clinical protocols, utilizing medical-grade laser technology and individualized treatment plans based on each patient's skin type, hair characteristics and clinical assessment. The practice also maintains LegitScript Healthcare Certification.

The statewide campaign represents a significant milestone in Refresh's continued expansion and reinforces its commitment to advancing a more transparent, accessible and patient-centered standard within the medical aesthetics industry.

Refresh operates offices in Jupiter, Wellington, Port St. Lucie, Vero Beach, Fort Lauderdale, Tampa, Brandon, St. Petersburg and Palm Harbor, with laser hair removal available at every location.

Campaign details, treatment pricing and office information are available at https://refreshmedical.com/byebush.

The initiative runs as long as the billboards are still up and is limited to one credit per patient. Participation requires a My Refresh account, available on iOS and Android, and is subject to promotional terms and conditions.

Refresh – Aesthetics & Wellness is a physician-led, family-owned medical aesthetics and wellness practice with nine locations across Florida, including Jupiter, Wellington, Port St. Lucie, Vero Beach, Fort Lauderdale, Tampa, Brandon, St. Petersburg and Palm Harbor.

Refresh offers cosmetic injectables, dermal fillers, laser hair removal, advanced skin rejuvenation, body contouring, medical weight management, hormone replacement therapy, IV therapy and personalized wellness programs. releases.title: Americans cut holiday budgets by nearly $600, but shoppers who use AI and social media spend more: BMO Real Financial Progress Index
releases.body:
• The BMO Real Financial Progress Index finds Americans plan to spend $2,200 on average this holiday season, approximately $600 less than 2025 
  • Holiday travel spending drops $136 on average, while spending on decoration drops by 52% and entertaining drops by 28% 
  • Shoppers using AI or social media outspend those who don't, shelling out $2,745 and $3,639 respectively
  • BMO offers tips to continue financial progress through the holiday spending season

CHICAGO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- It's beginning to look a lot like… a more frugal 2026 holiday season. New data from the BMO Real Financial Progress Index reveals that Americans plan to spend $2,198 on average across the festive season, a nearly $600 drop from $2,755 in 2025.

From shrinking gift lists and skipping holiday travel to scaling back holiday gatherings, Americans are looking for ways to make the season merry without making their wallet miserable. With two in three (67%) Americans saying they have grown more concerned about inflation and the cost of living in the past three months, the shift toward a more modest holiday is hardly surprising. 

"The end of the year should be a time of celebration, but after a prolonged period of rising costs, many people feel caught between enjoying the season and protecting their financial progress," said Robin Growley, U.S. Head of Consumer Products, BMO. "A clear budget and shopping list can help. AI and social media may make finding the right gift easier, but your financial goals – not your social feed – should determine what makes it into your cart."

Increased concerns over rising everyday costs have consumers trimming their holiday spending more than the tree. Americans are scaling back most on costs related to celebrations, with planned spending falling sharply across several categories compared with 2025:

  • Decorations: $53, a 52% decrease from $111 in 2025
  • Alcohol: $82, a 36% decrease from $129
  • Entertaining: $149, a 28% decrease from $205

The holiday-belt tightening extends well beyond twinkle lights and eggnog with Americans also cutting back across several other seasonal spending categories:

  • Travel: $354, a 28% decrease from $490
  • Groceries: $469, a 20% decrease from $587
  • Clothing: $189, a 24% decrease from $250
  • Electronic gifts: $168, a 24% decrease from $222
  • Dining out: $184, a 17% decrease from $223
  • Toys and games: $102, a 14% decrease from $118

While holiday budgets may be less merry, tighter purse strings help calm seasonal spending anxiety: 49% say that holiday spending is causing financial stress this year, compared to 53% who said the same in 2025.

However, if concerns about everyday costs are leading to lower spending, it may also be inspiring more generosity for those less fortunate. In the spirit of giving, Americans are increasing end-of-year charitable donations, estimating they will give $235 on average compared to just $202 last year.

More sleighs are staying grounded – and carrying fewer gifts

One reason behind that drop in overall holiday spending? More Americans are choosing to stay home for the holidays. Just three in 10 Americans will spend on travel during the 2026 holidays, a 10-percentage-point drop from last year.

In fact, Americans increasingly say they don't travel at all over the festive season. Compared to 2025, more people say they don't plan international (65% vs. 57%), domestic (48% vs. 43%), or even local (35% vs. 32%) travel during the holidays.

When it comes to what's waiting under the tree, Americans will have fewer presents there this winter. Nearly three in four (73%) say they plan to buy fewer gifts. One in three will purchase fewer gifts and spend less than in 2025, while another 40% plan to spend the same as last year but expect to get less for their money.

Even those with deeper pockets are planning a more modest holiday season this year: 64% of Americans with $250,000 or more in investable assets say they will purchase fewer gifts this year.

Despite the lower overall price tag, many Americans will be nursing a holiday spending hangover. Sixty percent of Americans will do their holiday shopping using payment methods that carry debt such as credit cards or "buy now, pay later," and nearly six in 10 (59%) Americans expect to carry at least some holiday spending debt into the New Year. On average, these Americans will have $1,238 in holiday-related spending debt to manage in 2027. Two in five (42%) Americans, including 54% of Gen Z and Millennials, say they are more likely to carry credit card debt after the holidays than any other time of year.

"A little planning can take a lot of stress out of the season," said Growley. "Whether it's talking with loved ones to set limits on gifts, starting a holiday fund to begin saving earlier in the year, or adjusting travel plans to avoid peak prices, small decisions can help you enjoy the season while staying on track with your financial goals."

The click-to-cart creep: Santa's new shopping assistants may be costing Americans more

For those trying to do more with less, technology is a growing tool in Santa's workshop for finding the perfect present and hunting down the hottest deals. Just over half of Americans plan to use AI to support their holiday shopping: 

  • 41% will use AI to research specific products and compare prices
  • 37% will use AI to identify the best holiday sales 
  • 37% will get help brainstorming gift ideas

While AI may be helping Americans find the perfect present, it might not actually be helping them find the perfect price. While one-third (33%) of Americans expect the technology will help them stick closer to a budget, Americans who plan to use AI for holiday shopping outspend those who don't by more than $1,000 ($2,745 vs. $1,643). 

With ever-evolving technology, AI agents can now do more than provide recommendations, some can make purchases on shoppers' behalf. But many Americans aren't quite ready to fully hand over the holiday shopping reins. Just 21% of shoppers say they will authorize an agent to make purchases for them. In fact, 38% express concern that a shopping agent will lead them to overspend. BMO recommends that consumers should never share sensitive banking information, including passwords, PINs or verification codes, through unauthorized channels, including AI agents.

Scrolling into a spending spree: Social media shoppers expect to spend nearly $1,600 more 

AI isn't the only digital influence shaping holiday spending patterns. Social media platforms will also have significant influence on how Americans spend this holiday season, particularly for younger generations.

Nearly half of Gen Z (47%) say influencers on social media are important in guiding their holiday purchases. Younger shoppers are also more likely to skip the traditional checkout and shop directly through social platforms. While just one in ten Americans say they will shop for holiday gifts directly on social media, that number rises to 19% for Gen Z and 17% for Millennials.

But those picture-perfect holiday posts may come with a less-than-perfect price tag. Americans who shop for the holidays on social media will spend significantly more this winter, estimating their holiday season will cost $3,639 compared to $2,035 for those who don't shop on social media, and 67% admitting they lose track of holiday spending while shopping directly via social platforms.

With social media shoppers three times as likely to say influencers guide their holiday shopping decisions (57% vs. 19%), it's possible those grid-worthy outfits and holiday parties are inspiring more than just holiday wish lists. Social shoppers expect to spend nearly three times as much on clothing ($439 vs. $160) and nearly four times as much on holiday decorations ($147 vs. $43).

"A quick search for the perfect gift can turn into a much bigger shopping cart than planned. The click-to-cart creep is very real, so consider using the '24-hour rule' of leaving an item in your cart and coming back to it the next day to make sure it isn't an impulsive purchase," Growley said.

All they want for Christmas is more money in the bank 

With the cost of living concerning many, Americans are setting boundaries to keep holiday budgets in check. From gift-giving ground rules to getting ahead of January bills, here's how they're trying to keep their finances merry and bright:

  • "No, really, you shouldn't have": Sometimes the best gift is no gift at all: 57% of Americans are discouraging their family from buying gifts so they can save money. For some, it's also a way to take the pressure off gift-giving: 40% say that they feel pressure to match what their loved ones spend on gifts.
  • Give the gift of a debt-free January: While most Americans are purchasing presents with IOUs, more shoppers are making a plan to pay off holiday bills sooner. Nearly half (48%) say they will pay off their holiday debt in a month or less, compared to 42% last year.
  • The best holiday present is a savings boost: Americans are doing a better job of keeping their future financial goals on their wish lists. Just 35% are knowingly sacrificing their long-term financial outlook to afford their winter spending, down from 42% last year.

Making real financial progress this holiday season

For Americans looking to keep their finances merry and bright this season, BMO offers the following tips to help make the most of the season without starting the New Year in the red:

  • Make budgets as loud as the celebrations: While not everyone will want to tell their loved ones to skip the presents, being open about a goal to spend less can take the pressure off. Encourage friends and family to join in "loud budgeting" by agreeing on spending limits, setting gift expectations or finding fun, low-cost ways to celebrate.
  • Don't get lost in the blizzard of sales: A deal isn't a deal if it leads to spending more than planned. 47% of Americans say they spend more than they intend to while hunting for holiday sales and discounts. To avoid overspending from sale-hopping, build a budget and a shopping list and stick to it. 
  • Use points to add travel back to the festive budget: To add travel back into holiday plans next year, using a credit card such as the BMO Escape Credit Card can turn day-to-day spending into points that can help make holiday travel more affordable.
  • Start building a 2027 holiday fund: Preparing for a big jump in spending at the end of the year is a challenge for many. To save more for the holiday season, BMO's digital banking tools make it easy to create and name a holiday fund, set a savings goal, automate monthly transfers, and track progress. 
  • Get a guide for the financial sleigh: If it feels like flying through a financial fog this holiday season, a financial navigation tool like the DollarGPS app can help project how a big holiday trip or a generous gift for loved ones can fit in one's broader financial journey.
  • Think about an old school holiday shopping strategy: Digital tools can make shopping easier, but often scrolling a little less means a little less spending. Americans who do not plan to use AI or social media to shop this season will spend just $1,640 on average. A more manual approach to finding and purchasing gifts might help keep better track of holiday spending.

To learn more about how BMO can help Americans make real financial progress this holiday season, visit https://www.bmo.com/us.

About the BMO Real Financial Progress Index

Launched in February 2021, the BMO Real Financial Progress Index is an indicator of how consumers feel about their personal finances and whether they are making financial progress. The survey aims to spark dialogue that will help consumers reach their financial goals and to humanize a topic that causes anxiety for many: money.

The research detailed in this document was conducted by Ipsos in the U.S. from Aug. 31, 2026, to Oct. 6, 2026. A sample of n=2,500 adults ages 18+ in the U.S. were collected via the Ipsos panel. Quotas and weighting were used to ensure the sample's composition reflects that of the American population according to census parameters. This survey has a credibility interval of +/- 2.4 per cent or 19 times out of 20, of what the results would have been had all American adults 18+ been surveyed.

About BMO Financial Group 

BMO Financial Group is the eighth largest bank in North America by assets, with total assets of $1.5 trillion as of July 31, 2026. Serving clients for more than 200 years, BMO provides a broad range of personal and commercial banking, wealth management, global markets and investment banking products and services across Canada, the United States, and select markets globally. BMO is innovating for business value, by deploying and integrating human, digital and artificial intelligence to personalize client experiences, augment teams, and automate its business responsibly. Driven by its purpose, to Boldly Grow the Good in business and life, BMO is committed to driving positive change in the world, and making progress for a thriving economy, sustainable future, and stronger communities.

releases.body:
Integration connects streaming TV, video, audio and display campaigns to inbound calls, texts and form submissions, giving advertisers greater visibility into campaign performance and ROI

ATLANTA, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CallRail, the AI-powered lead engagement platform used by more than 225,000 businesses and 7,000 marketing agencies, today announced an integration with Amazon Ads to help advertisers better understand how their streaming TV, online video, audio, and display ads drive customer inquiries and business results.

The integration helps advertisers measure inbound calls, texts, and form submissions that may occur days after an ad is seen or heard, giving businesses and agencies a clearer view of which campaigns generate valuable leads. These customer interactions are automatically recorded as conversions in Amazon Ads, providing advertisers with more actionable insights into campaign performance and helping them make smarter decisions about where to invest their advertising dollars.

"A click only tells you so much. If you're a roofer or a personal injury attorney, you want to know whether your advertising is actually bringing in customers," said Marc Ginsberg, CEO of CallRail. "That's been difficult to measure with streaming and video ads, particularly when someone responds by picking up the phone. Our integration with Amazon Ads gives businesses a better way to see which campaigns are driving leads and where their advertising dollars are making an impact."

When a consumer who has seen an Amazon Ads ad later calls, texts or submits a form, CallRail sends a conversion signal to Amazon Ads, where it can be matched to an eligible ad impression and attributed to the corresponding campaign. The integration is built directly to Amazon Ads, requires no third-party tools, and allows advertisers to:

  • Measure campaign performance: See which ads generate inbound calls, with reporting across campaigns, creative, audiences, and geographic locations.
  • Optimize campaigns in real time: See which ads and audiences drive high-intent leads and adjust campaign spending accordingly. 
  • Consolidate conversion reporting: View inbound calls, texts, and form submissions together within Amazon Ads, reducing the need to reconcile performance data across platforms.

"For local advertisers, a phone call is often one of the most valuable customer actions", said Lily Tong, Director of Brand and Cross-Channel Measurement, Amazon Ads. "The integration with CallRail helps advertisers see which Amazon Ads campaigns drive real-world calls, texts, and form submissions, and is designed to provide the closed-loop measurement they need to prove ROI and optimize with confidence."

The integration also supports Amazon's AI-driven campaign optimization, including Performance+ campaigns. By adding inbound inquiries alongside online conversions, it provides signals that can help inform automated bidding and audience optimization, particularly for businesses whose customer inquiries often happen offline.

About CallRail 

CallRail is the lead engagement platform that makes it easy for businesses to attract more leads, convert more customers, and optimize their marketing. Serving more than 225,000 businesses worldwide, CallRail's AI-powered solutions help businesses attribute each call, text, chat, and form to their marketing journey, use insights from their conversations to better understand their buyers, and eliminate missed opportunities with AI that can handle lead interactions 24/7. 

CallRail has grown from the G2 top-rated inbound call tracking solution to include Form Tracking, Premium Conversation Intelligence™ and Voice Assist. CallRail's award-winning platform integrates with thousands of leading marketing and sales software, and offers affiliate, agency, and technology partnership opportunities, helping businesses earn, grow, and build with CallRail. For more information, visit http://www.callrail.com.

releases.body:
Industry leader recognized for his lasting impact on media measurement and collaboration

NEW YORK, Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Advertising Research Foundation (ARF) has posthumously honored Andy Brown, former chairman and chief executive at Kantar Media, with its highest distinction, the Erwin Ephron Demystification Award, recognizing his exceptional contributions to media measurement, thought leadership and industry collaboration. The award was presented at the ASI conference in Venice, Italy, marking the first time the honor has been awarded posthumously or presented outside an ARF event.

Throughout his distinguished career, Brown helped guide the media research industry through decades of transformation. His longstanding involvement with the Worldwide Readership Research Symposium (WRRS), later the Print and Digital Research Forum (PDRF), which he cosponsored on behalf of Kantar Media, reflected his commitment to advancing measurement practices and fostering dialogue among industry leaders.

Beyond his professional accomplishments, Brown was widely admired for his intellectual curiosity, generosity and ability to unite people across competing organizations and disciplines. Following his passing, the ARF hosted a memorial in New York City in July, drawing tributes from measurement competitors, agencies, broadcasters and digital platforms alike.

"Andy believed that even in an industry filled with competing interests and differing perspectives, we could find common ground and work toward meaningful solutions," said Scott McDonald, President and CEO of the ARF. "His greatest legacy is the community he helped build and the spirit of collaboration he inspired."

Named for pioneering advertising thinker Erwin Ephron, the award recognizes individuals who challenge conventional wisdom, simplify complex ideas and advance the scientific practice of advertising and marketing.

Brown is the award's 13th recipient, joining distinguished industry leaders including Howard Shimmel, Helen Katz, Artie Bulgrin, and inaugural recipient Bill Harvey.

Brown's children, Alex and Rory Brown, traveled from London to Venice to accept the award on his behalf.

About the ARF

Founded in 1936, the Advertising Research Foundation (ARF) is the leading organization dedicated to creating better advertising through research, standards and collaboration. With more than 400 member companies, the ARF advances the science and practice of advertising, media and marketing.

For more information, visit thearf.org or follow the ARF on LinkedIn, YouTube, X and Facebook.

releases.body:
• AI-supported tool helps find fake content that could mislead customers
  • Three steps help customers protect their money: spot it, check it and report it

CHARLOTTE, N.C., Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Duke Energy has removed hundreds of fake websites, social media accounts and online ads since November 2025 as part of an expanded effort to protect customers from increasingly sophisticated utility scams.

Many of these scams are designed to look like legitimate Duke Energy content, directing customers to fake payment pages and phone numbers.

Ahead of Utility Scam Awareness Day on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, Duke Energy, Piedmont Natural Gas and the Better Business Bureau are sharing three steps customers can use anytime something doesn't feel right to protect their money and personal information: spot it, check it and report it.

"If something doesn't feel right, take a moment to check your account at duke-energy.com, in the Duke Energy app or with the number on your bill, and report anything suspicious," said Jessica Bednarcik, senior vice president of customer services operations at Duke Energy.

How is Duke Energy helping protect customers from fake online content?

Utility scams often begin when customers searching online for help find a fake customer service number posted across websites, social media, ads or apps. Duke Energy's AI-supported tool scans websites, social media and paid ads for fake Duke Energy content, including impostor helplines. When the tool finds suspected scam content, Duke Energy works with the website or social media platform hosting it to have it removed.

In North Carolina, customers reported more than a thousand scam attempts to Duke Energy from January through September 2026.

How can customers spot, check and report a utility scam?

  • Step 1 – Spot it: Pause when something doesn't look right, especially when there is pressure to act now.
  • Step 2 – Check it: Use the phone number or website on your Duke Energy or Piedmont Natural Gas bill – not a link, QR code or number from a search result or message.
  • Step 3 – Report it: Don't engage. Save the message, receipt or screenshot, then use Duke Energy's Scam Reporting Tool or call Piedmont Natural Gas to report the suspicious content. NEW YORK, Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ScareScore, the biometric entertainment platform that turns an audience's physical reactions into a personal score, today announced a partnership with Paranormal Activity, the smash-hit, sold-out, critically acclaimed production currently playing on Broadway at the August Wilson Theatre. Beginning on November 19 and continuing through the production's final February 28, 2027 performance, theatergoers wearing a compatible smartwatch can opt-in, free to measure their body's responses to the show's scares, then compare their ScareScore with friends after the curtain falls. The partnership marks ScareScore's first move from the screen to the stage, demonstrating that the most telling review of a live experience is the one your body writes while it's happening.

"A review tells you what someone thought after the show – ScareScore shows you what your body did during it," said Chris Anastas, Founder and CEO of ScareScore. "Your watch reads your heart rate and movement, we match those reactions to the moments that caused them, and when the curtain comes down, you get a score that shows how hard the experience hit you."

James and Lou move from Chicago to London to escape their past, but they soon discover that places aren't haunted, people are… With an original story inspired by the film franchise, Paranormal Activity reimagines the modern ghost story with an intimacy that only live theatre can provide. Written by Levi Holloway and directed by Felix Barrett Paranormal Activity stars Cher Álvarez as Lou, Travis A. Knight as James, Shannon Cochran as Carolanne, and Eva Kaminsky as Etheline Cotgrave.

"Paranormal Activity is built on tension that you can cut with a knife: those long, silent stretches where an entire theater is holding its breath – and that's exactly what ScareScore was made to capture, and there's no bigger stage for that kind of experience than Broadway," said JP Ouellette, Co-Founder of ScareScore and producer of the Sundance drama Mass. "For a live theater production like Paranormal Activity, ScareScore represents a new way to connect with an audience and to understand exactly where a story lands. Part of what makes this so exciting for us is that it doesn't stop at Broadway. The same idea works anywhere people gather to feel something together: a movie premiere, a series finale watch party, a haunted attraction, a concert – every live experience is about to have a scoreboard, and the audience gets to keep the score."

Tapping the power of ScareScore requires theatergoers download the free ScareScore app on an iPhone paired with an Apple Watch, or an Android phone paired with a Wear OS smartwatch, and op-in before the show and complete the required setup with their account. During the performance, the phone stays silent and the watch goes dark in Movie Mode, so nothing lights up, buzzes, or distracts the cast or the people in the next seat, and no one can check or game a score mid-show. Users can pause the session during intermission.After the curtain call, each guest's ScareScore is revealed, showing which moments hit the hardest and how their reaction stacks up against friend and the rest of the night's audience.

Paranormal Activity is playing a strictly limited engagement on Broadway through February 28, 2027 only. Tickets are available at paranormalbroadway.com and at the August Wilson Theatre box office.

releases.title: IAB Releases AI-Era Attribution Blueprint, Giving the Industry a Shared Way to Account for AI's Role in Purchases
releases.body:
New Framework Classifies How AI Shapes and Completes Conversions, Defines Who Is Eligible to Make a Claim and What Evidence Is Required, and Calls on the Ecosystem to Help Narrow the Measurement Gap

NEW YORK, Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB), the leading trade organization for the digital advertising industry, today released the AI-Era Attribution Blueprint, a new framework that gives the industry a shared way to classify AI's role in a conversion and evaluate which parties can claim credit for it. The release comes as ad buyers name comparing AI-driven and traditional customer journeys as their top measurement challenge (45%), and 44% rely on branded search and direct traffic as proxies for AI influence they can't track, according to IAB's 2026 Outlook Study: September Update.

"As AI takes on more of the purchase journey, from sparking interest to completing the sale, the clicks and referrals that attribution depends on are thinning out or disappearing," said Caroline Giegerich, VP, AI, IAB. "AI-influenced sales are sometimes reported as search or direct traffic, which can send the next marketing investment to the wrong channel. The AI-Era Attribution Blueprint works alongside existing attribution systems, defining the additional credit claims AI creates and the evidence each one requires."

The AI-Era Attribution Blueprint asks who or what created the intent, made the decision and completed the purchase, then classifies each conversion as Human-Owned, AI-Assisted or AI-Executed. That pathway determines which parties are eligible for a decision claim or a contributory claim, if any, and what evidence each claim requires. A claim is not credit; it is the right to be evaluated for credit.

A Call to Action for the Industry

Much of the evidence needed to support those claims is either not captured or sits inside AI platforms. The AI-Era Attribution Blueprint calls on each part of the ecosystem to help narrow that gap:

  • Brands can estimate the share of their conversions in each pathway.
  • AI platforms can disclose whether recommendations are paid or organic and what sources informed them, and can label AI-originated traffic consistently.
  • Agencies can apply a single  claim-and-evidence standard across platforms, separating platform-reported claims from independently verified ones.
  • Publishers can identify the contributory claims their content creates and the evidence needed to support them.

"Attribution has never given us a complete view of how influence becomes an outcome, and AI adds new dimensions to the challenge," said David Cohen, CEO, IAB. "The AI-Era Attribution Blueprint is honest about what the industry can't yet substantiate, and we're inviting everyone in the ecosystem to apply it and help make AI's role in commerce more observable, verifiable, and measurable."



As an industry convener, IAB will bring brands, agencies, AI platforms, retailers, and publishers together to share what they're learning as more data becomes available, and to keep moving the industry forward in narrowing these measurement gaps.

The AI-Era Attribution Blueprint was developed by the IAB AI-Era Attribution Blueprint Working Group, a cross-industry team of brand, agency, publisher, AI platform, and measurement leaders. It builds on IAB's Measuring Visibility in the AI Era playbook by extending that work from how brands show up in AI platforms to how that presence connects to sales.

To access the AI-Era Attribution Blueprint, visit https://www.iab.com/guidelines/the-ai-era-attribution-blueprint/ 

About IAB

The Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB) empowers the media and marketing industries to thrive in the digital economy. Its membership comprises more than 700 leading media companies, brands, agencies, and the technology firms responsible for selling, delivering, and optimizing digital ad marketing campaigns. The trade group fields critical research on interactive advertising, while also educating brands, agencies, and the wider business community on the importance of digital marketing. In affiliation with the IAB Tech Lab, IAB develops technical standards and solutions. IAB is committed to professional development and elevating the knowledge, skills, expertise, and collaboration of the workforce across the industry. Through the work of its public policy office in Washington, D.C., the trade association advocates for its members and promotes the value of the interactive advertising industry to legislators and policymakers. releases.title: IAB Tech Lab Announces OM SDK Support for Emerging CTV Ad Formats
releases.body:
Expanded Open Measurement Support Brings Consistent Impression Measurement to Pause, Menu, Screensaver, and Overlay Ads Across Connected TV

NEW YORK, Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- IAB Tech Lab, the global digital advertising technical standards-setting body, today announced expanded Open Measurement SDK (OM SDK) support for emerging connected TV (CTV) ad formats included in the CTV Ad Portfolio. The release enables impression measurement for Pause, Menu (also known as Homescreen), Screensaver, and Overlay Ads, extending established measurement capabilities to formats that are creating new monetization opportunities across CTV.

"CTV advertising is moving fast, and measurement has to move with it," said Jill Wittkopp, VP of Product, IAB Tech Lab. "The idea that everything on a TV screen is automatically viewable because it is CTV just does not hold up anymore. We have new formats, new placements, and new ways for consumers to experience advertising, so the industry needs measurement that can tell us what is actually happening on that screen."

The dollars moving into streaming make that measurement increasingly important. U.S. digital video ad spending is projected to surpass $80 billion in 2026, growing 11% year over year and nearly 20% faster than the overall ad market, while digital video will account for more than 60% of total TV and video ad spend for the first time. CTV remains one of the market's fastest-growing channels, with IAB projecting 13.8% growth in CTV ad spend in 2026. As publishers and platforms look to build new revenue streams beyond traditional pre-roll and mid-roll advertising, formats such as Pause, Menu, Screensaver, and Overlay Ads create new opportunities to monetize the CTV screen.

These emerging formats also introduce new questions about where an ad appears and how much of the screen it occupies, beyond the traditional assumption of CTV always being viewable. Some of these new CTV Ad formats enable flexibility in how much screen real estate is used. Standardized measurement gives buyers greater confidence in what they are buying and gives sellers a stronger foundation to bring that inventory to market at scale.

"As CTV expands beyond traditional video ad formats, advertisers need consistent, independent measurement that reflects how those ads are actually experienced on screen," said Todd Randak, General Manager, CTV at DoubleVerify. "Extending Open Measurement to emerging formats is an important step toward giving advertisers greater transparency into media quality and helping the industry build confidence as new CTV inventory scales."

"Pause ads offer a premium canvas, and now the infrastructure needs to catch up," said David Dworin, Chief Product Officer, FreeWheel. "Standardized bidding signals and consistent measurement help buyers understand what they're buying and how it performs—reducing friction and building confidence to scale pause ads and future formats."

"New CTV formats like pause and menu ads create new opportunities for advertisers, but their on-screen behavior makes them difficult to measure. OMSDK for CTV will help enable consistent, independent verification so advertisers and publishers can invest in these formats with confidence" added Gautam Babbar, Sr. Director, Product Management at IAS.

"As connected TV continues to grow and command higher CPMs, consistent and transparent measurement becomes increasingly critical. Expanding OM SDK support to emerging ad formats—including Pause, Menu, Screensaver, and Overlay Ads—is an important step," said Ron Pinelli, SVP Digital Research and Standards Media Rating Council. "Broad adoption of OM SDK benefits both advertisers and publishers by enabling more consistent impression measurement, strengthening trust, and reducing fragmentation across proprietary measurement solutions."

The expanded OM SDK support helps unlock the commercial potential of emerging CTV formats by giving buyers and sellers a common measurement foundation. As emerging formats like Pause and Menu Ads gain traction and move toward greater programmatic scale, publishers and platforms have an opportunity to open new revenue streams beyond the traditional commercial break and attract budgets that increasingly flow through programmatic channels. With consistent measurement in place, these emerging experiences have a clearer path from new ad format to scalable CTV inventory.

To learn more about OM SDK for CTV support for emerging CTV ad formats and how to get started with planning to implement, visit https://iabtechlab.com/omsdk

About IAB Technology Laboratory

Established in 2014, the IAB Technology Laboratory (Tech Lab) is a non-profit consortium that engages a member community globally to develop foundational technology and standards that enable growth and trust in the digital media ecosystem. Comprised of digital publishers, ad technology firms, agencies, brands, and other member companies, IAB Tech Lab focuses on solutions for brand safety and ad fraud; identity, data, and consumer privacy; cross-channel programmatic effectiveness and ad measurement; and the impact of LLMs and AI agents on advertising. Its work includes the OpenRTB real-time bidding protocol, ads.txt anti-fraud specification, Open Measurement SDK for viewability and verification, VAST video specification, Trusted Server, and the Agentic Roadmap initiative for agentic advertising. Board members and companies are listed at https://iabtechlab.com/about-the-iab-tech-lab/tech-lab-leadership/. For more information, please visit https://iabtechlab.com.

releases.title: IAB Launches Trusted Creator Brand Deal Initiative to Build the Infrastructure Behind the Creator Economy's Next Phase of Growth
releases.body:
New Research Identifies Seven Opportunity Areas, From a Common Definition of a "View" to Fee Disclosure

NEW YORK, Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Creator media budgets are expected to reach $44 billion this year, but the systems for measuring, contracting, and paying creators have not kept pace. Today, the Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB), the leading trade organization for the digital advertising ecosystem, released The Creator Economy's Next Chapter, the first research report from its Trusted Creator Brand Deal Initiative. The report identifies seven opportunity areas for the industry to address challenges that could slow the creator economy growth.

The research confirms gaps the creator ecosystem  has long recognized, and the Initiative moves immediately from findings to action. IAB's Creator Economy Board and committee will now form targeted working groups to address measurement standards. The measure of success is a simple shift: when industry leaders are surveyed in the future by similar research, the obstacles at the top of their list should look completely different than they do today.

"Creator marketing has largely won the argument about whether it belongs in the marketing plan. What it needs now is the infrastructure to scale," said James Douglas, VP, Experience Center, IAB. "The people closest to this work told us where the friction is, and more than half said they would help build the solutions."

Seven Opportunity Areas  for a Stronger Creator Economy

Drawn from two waves of research by the IAB Creator Economy Board and FrontRow Research, including a survey of 53 industry leaders, the findings are directional, but their message is consistent. The aim is not to standardize creators or set prices, but to build shared definitions and expectations that let buyers, sellers, and measurement partners compete and innovate on a common foundation.

The research data pointed to seven opportunity areas for the industry to consider:

  • Fix measurement at its foundation: 67% named measurement as the top problem, and a common definition of a "view" was the most-requested standard (66%).
  • Model contract clauses: Usage rights are the top friction clause (61%).
  • Consider the benefits of prompt payment terms: 60% agree longer payment terms cause cascading harm, and only 6% disagree.
  • Equip senior leaders and finance with an evaluation playbook: 94% report at least occasional conflict with senior leadership over creator decisions, with budget allocation hit hardest.
  • Propose optimal brand operating models: 80% agree media and creator buyers work independently, often limiting the full value of creator campaigns.
  • Make performance data easier to share: 58% say withheld results limit shared learning, though access and data quality are cited almost as often as withholding.
  • Make fee disclosure the default: 74% agree opacity persists partly because some in the industry benefit from it, and the report calls on buyers to lead fee disclosure efforts.

IAB Prioritizes Measurement Standards in 2027

IAB will work to define core metrics across platforms, from views to impressions, reach, and watch time, and will build a Creator advisory body to guide the work, in line with the IAB Experience Center's 2027 roadmap.

Working alongside the Media Rating Council (MRC) and engaged industry bodies, IAB plans to convene platforms and measurement providers to establish common definitions for views, impressions, reach, and watch time. This work will lay the foundation for more consistent reporting and help brands and agencies better evaluate creator marketing performance across platforms.

"The creator economy has grown up faster than the infrastructure to support it, and the window to act is now, while demand is strong and the industry is willing," said David Cohen, CEO, IAB. "If we wait, the same friction points will get set in stone and undoubtedly inhibit future growth."

IAB is inviting creators, brands, agencies, platforms, publishers, ad tech partners, commerce and retail media teams, legal teams, measurement providers and talent representatives to join the Initiative's working groups and help shape the standards.

To download The Creator Economy's Next Chapter and get involved, click here.

About IAB

The Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB) empowers the media and marketing industries to thrive in the digital economy. Its membership comprises more than 700 leading media companies, brands, agencies, and the technology firms responsible for selling, delivering, and optimizing digital ad marketing campaigns. The trade group fields critical research on interactive advertising, while also educating brands, agencies, and the wider business community on the importance of digital marketing. In affiliation with the IAB Tech Lab, IAB develops technical standards and solutions. IAB is committed to professional development and elevating the knowledge, skills, expertise, and collaboration of the workforce across the industry. Through the work of its public policy office in Washington, D.C., the trade association advocates for its members and promotes the value of the interactive advertising industry to legislators and policymakers. Founded in 1996, IAB is headquartered in New York City.

releases.title: New National Study Finds Youth Sports Sponsorship Outperforms Traditional Advertising in Building Parent Trust
releases.body:
Priority Partnerships research conducted by YouGov Sport finds surprising advantages for youth sports sponsorship compared with professional sports and traditional advertising

PORTLAND, Ore., Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A new national study finds that youth sports parents are more likely to trust brands sponsoring their children's sports programs than brands advertising through traditional channels. The findings suggest an opportunity to attract more corporate investment into youth sports, potentially helping programs offset rising costs for families. 

Key findings from the Priority Partnerships Youth Sports Sponsorship Study:

  • Brand Trust: 68% say sponsorship of their child's sports program would make them likely to trust a brand, compared with 47% for TV commercials and 38% for influencer posts.
  • Brand Consideration: 71% say they would consider a brand named an Official Partner of their child's sports program, compared with 56% when the brand is an Official Partner of their favorite professional team.
  • Brand Trial: 64% say sponsorship of their child's sports program would make them likely to try a company they've never used before, compared with 51% for professional sports sponsorship and 49% for college sponsorship.

"There's a difference between seeing a company's advertisement and seeing that company support something that's important to your kids and family," said Dan Scheinman, President of Priority Partnerships. "Now we have research that shows how parents respond to that support."

As jersey sponsorships draw increased attention in professional and college sports, the research points to a potentially overlooked opportunity in youth sports. More than three-quarters (77%) of parents say they would be more likely to remember a sponsor on their child's uniform than one on the uniform of a professional sports team they follow.

The findings also have implications beyond marketing. As families and youth sports organizations contend with the rising costs of participation, corporate sponsorship represents a potential source of funding that could help support programs and reduce their reliance on registration fees.

"One of the reasons we commissioned this research is that we believe there's an opportunity to bring more corporate investment into youth sports," Scheinman said. "If brands can see the marketing value of supporting these programs, there's a stronger business case for investing in them. That has the potential to benefit the sponsors, youth sports operators, and the families these programs serve."

The complete Priority Partnerships Youth Sports Sponsorship Study is available free of charge at: www.prioritypartnerships.com/sponsorshipinyouthsportsreport.

About the Study

The study was conducted by YouGov Sport among 1,004 U.S. parents ages 25-54 with children under 18 participating in organized sports. The online survey was fielded August 27-September 3, 2026.

releases.body:
Competitive Renewal Launches New Era of Digital, Experiential and Branded Media as ECP Undergoes Major Terminal Expansion

PANAMA CITY, Fla., Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Clear Channel Outdoor (CCO)'s Airports Division, the leading U.S. airport sponsorship and advertising partner, has renewed and expanded its longstanding partnership with Northwest Florida Beaches International Airport (ECP). Originally established in 2005 and reselected through a competitive process, the renewed agreement reflects two decades of operational performance and the airport's confidence in CCO's ability to deliver on its next chapter of growth.

The agreement comes as ECP undertakes a major terminal expansion and modernization project, creating an opportunity for CCO to invest more into the airport's advertising program with new digital media, experiential activations and refreshed displays. The centerpiece of the new program will be a network of double-sided digital flags throughout the concourse, introducing dynamic content and a contemporary digital media presence that integrates seamlessly and enhances the terminal environment.

Under the new agreement, CCO will make a significant investment in ECP's advertising infrastructure over an initial three-year contract term and with the opportunity to renew. The investment will support the evolution of a curated and contemporary advertising program, with strategically positioned state-of-the-art media that complements the passenger experience and the airport's sense of place. The program will provide greater flexibility for advertisers while creating new opportunities for brands to engage travelers and support ECP's long-term commercial growth.

"ECP is a market that performs well above its size, and this renewal is a reflection of what a strong collaborative partnership produces over time," said Morten Gotterup, president, Clear Channel Outdoor's Airports Division. "As ECP invests in the next generation of its terminal, we have an opportunity to invest into that experience and to build something that reflects both where this airport is today and where it's headed. Our new program will bring together digital, experiential and high-impact media to continue to delight passengers and the brands that want to reach them for years to come."

ECP has experienced sustained growth since opening in 2010, serving a record 1.9 million passengers in 2025 representing a 3.1% year-over-year increase. The airport serves large, leisure-oriented audiences, with travelers visiting Northwest Florida's Emerald Coast for vacations, weekend getaways and outdoor recreation. Through nonstop and seasonal service from American, Delta, Southwest and United Airlines, ECP connects the region with major markets including Atlanta, Nashville, Dallas, Denver, Houston, New York, Chicago and Baltimore. That traveler profile—arriving and ready to engage—makes ECP a compelling platform for brands looking to connect with consumers at the start of their trip.

"As ECP undergoes this major Terminal Expansion, we are focused on enhancing every element of the traveler experience. Clear Channel's commitment to investing in state-of-the-art digital infrastructure and experiential activations will not only modernize our concourses but also provide powerful new avenues for local and national brands to connect with our growing passenger base. We are proud to build upon our history together and look forward to a new era of innovation that supports ECP's long-term commercial vitality," stated ECP Executive Director Parker W. McClellan Jr., A.A.E.

The renewed partnership reflects CCO and ECP's shared commitment to evolving the airport experience alongside the continued growth of Northwest Florida. As construction progresses toward the terminal expansion's 2029 completion, the new advertising program will provide a flexible platform that grows with the airport creating new opportunities for brands to connect with travelers while supporting ECP's long-term revenue goals.

To learn more about Clear Channel Airports, visit https://clearchanneloutdoor.com/airport-advertising/.

Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. is at the forefront of driving innovation in the out-of-home advertising industry. Our dynamic advertising platform is broadening the pool of advertisers using its medium through the expansion of digital billboards and displays and the integration of data analytics and programmatic capabilities that deliver measurable campaigns that are simpler to buy. By leveraging the scale, reach and flexibility of our diverse portfolio of assets, we connect advertisers with millions of consumers every month.

releases.title: Cuttable Unveils Next-Generation AI Advertising Platform as U.S. Expansion Accelerates
releases.body:
The platform's evolution comes alongside an A$20 million Series A funding round led by Airtree Ventures, marking Cuttable's next phase of growth as it moves beyond AI ad generation.

NEW YORK, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cuttable, an AI-powered creative production platform for performance marketing teams, today unveiled the next evolution of its platform, designed to help brands move beyond generating ads to understand what works and make smarter decisions about what to create next. Just one year after entering the U.S. market, the Australian-founded company now generates 40% of its revenue from the region.

While AI has made producing ads faster and easier, knowing which creative to make next remains a challenge. Most tools focus on either generating ads or analyzing their performance, leaving marketers to connect the dots between what they intend to test, what actually worked and what to create next.

Cuttable brings those pieces together. Its evolved platform connects a brand's creative assets, customer data and performance history with the marketer's original intent, building on what the brand has already tried rather than starting from scratch with each new creative brief.

Cuttable's software was built to remove creative as a bottleneck for performance marketing teams producing, testing and rebuilding ads at scale. The platform reads a brand's website, social channels and guidelines to build an editable brand strategy and brand kit. From there, marketers can write a brief in plain language and receive finished, editable ads, built using existing brand and product assets or Cuttable's AI content studio, Shoots, which creates and extends photo and video content.

Finished ads publish directly to Meta Ads Manager, and Cuttable's Ad Insights reads the performance back from Meta, including thumbstop, click-through rate and return on ad spend, so that the next brief builds on what worked. It's this continuous feedback loop, rather than creative generation alone, that differentiates Cuttable from tools that separately generate ads or report on performance. 

Cuttable's Co-founder & CEO, Sam Kroonenburg, who previously founded and sold A Cloud Guru in 2021, said, "Creative is still made the way it was thirty years ago, one ad at a time. Making an ad has never been the hard part, it is knowing which one to make next. We are building the creative production system ecommerce performance marketers have been waiting for."

Across 280,000 ads and more than $320 million in Meta spend run through its platform, Cuttable found that one ad in eleven returns ten times its spend or better, and that a small number of ads end up carrying an entire account. The company's data also shows brands increase creative output 3.4 times going into November, underscoring the growing pressure to produce and test ads at scale.

In just two years since launching, Cuttable now works with more than 420 brands across the United States, Australia, New Zealand, Asia and Europe, including lululemon, Rodan & Fields and Brick. Brands on the platform average a 4.4 times return on ad spend and see a 37 percent lift in account-level return on ad spend after moving to Cuttable. To support its growing U.S. business, Cuttable is actively hiring and building out its San Francisco team.

Airtree, which first invested in Cuttable earlier this year, returned to lead the round. One of Australia's largest technology investors, its portfolio includes Canva, Airwallex, Linktree and SafetyCulture.

Airtree Ventures partner James Cameron, whose firm also backed A Cloud Guru, said: "Since we backed Cuttable's seed round, their growth has been much faster than our (already very high) expectations. The world of ad creative is being turned on its head by AI, and we're excited to lead this round as Cuttable becomes the leading system that performance marketers reach for to make content work harder."

With the U.S. already emerging as a major growth market, Cuttable plans to use its latest funding to accelerate its expansion and advance the next evolution of its platform. Cuttable's focus from here is on closing the creative loop, helping marketers decide what to make next rather than only how to make it.

ABOUT CUTTABLE

Cuttable is a creative production platform for performance marketing teams, used by more than 420 brands across the United States, Australia, New Zealand, Asia and Europe. The company is headquartered in New York with offices in Melbourne and San Francisco.

To learn more, visit cuttable.com.

PHILADELPHIA, Oct. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- fullthrottle.ai®, a pioneer in first-party data media solutions and AdTech operating systems, today announced the launch of Audience Insights, a new reporting capability designed to give advertisers a clearer understanding of the content, shows, and entertainment their campaign audiences actually consume, and how those audiences spend time with their brand.

fullthrottle.ai® launches Audience Insights: see the shows, publishers, and markets your campaign audiences engage with.

Audience Insights brings key campaign intelligence into a simplified view, helping advertisers move beyond standard campaign delivery metrics to better understand the audiences they are reaching. Through Audience Insights, advertisers can uncover content and media consumption patterns across their campaigns, including the shows, programming, and entertainment their audiences engage with, the publishers and channels delivering that content, and the markets and ZIP codes where those audiences live.

That visibility is possible because of fullthrottle.ai's direct relationships with premium publishers, including Nexstar, iHeartMedia, TuneIn, Roku, Spectrum, SiriusXM (Pandora), Comcast Advertising, and TelevisaUnivision, combined with Immersive Household® delivery that connects a single household's behavior across CTV, audio, display, video, and direct mail. Advertisers buying those publishers directly, at a fixed CPM, typically do not get that same connected view of how their audience engages with their brand. Audience Insights also reflects activations available within the fullthrottle.ai® platform across additional premium publishers, including Warner Bros. Discovery, FOX, Spotify, Hearst, and AMP Media.

Most comparable reports in the category answer a narrower question: where the ads ran. That is a defensive screen, built to confirm delivery after the fact. Because Audience Insights is built on first-party data and SafeMatch® attribution, it answers a different question: where real shoppers and actual transacting customers are consuming media. Advertisers can see the placements, the channels, and the show-level content and domain-level destinations where their buyers spend time. fullthrottle.ai® believes the best defense is a good offense. These insights extend beyond a single campaign, giving advertisers a real psychographic view of real buyers that can inform media planning and buying across traditional and digital channels alike.

For multi-market advertisers, campaign-level reporting can also reveal differences between individual markets. Campaigns targeting different geographies can surface distinct publisher and media consumption patterns, giving advertisers a more localized view of audience behavior.

When advertisers set up individual markets as separate campaigns, each campaign has its own Audience Insights reporting. This allows advertisers to see market-specific differences, including local publishers and media consumption patterns, without combining the reporting across markets.

"Audience Insights is really about helping advertisers understand how an audience spends time with their brand," said Lou DiGiacomo, VP of Product at fullthrottle.ai®. "We've taken a number of different insights available within the platform and distilled them into a simple view that makes it easier for advertisers to understand what is happening across their campaigns."

Audience Insights also gives teams a practical way to bring these findings into ongoing campaign conversations. Reports can be exported as PDFs, while individual charts can be incorporated into presentations and reporting.

The addition of Audience Insights expands fullthrottle.ai's ability to help advertisers not only activate audiences across channels but also gain greater visibility into the media and market behaviors surrounding those audiences.

Audience Insights is available within the fullthrottle.ai® platform.
